messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: streaming-prod / model=redwood/gpt-small-int8-calib-2026-03 p99 latency > 3.0s for last 5m. SLO breach threshold hit. Link: https://monitoring.company/alerts/9876

Sara (SRE): I'm paged — joining. any quick context?

Mike (ML Eng): we pushed an int8 calibration profile 12m ago to streaming pool to cut memory. perf looked fine in staging, but prod p95/p99 jumped after rollout. spikes mainly on streaming and sessioned chat.

Anna (Oncall): CS reports 3 customer tickets flagged as timeouts/stalls: #1234, #1235, #1236. No full request failures, mostly prolonged stalls during streaming.

Ryan (Prod Eng): infra traces show requests stuck at "dequantize_kv_wait" for 200-600ms more than baseline. queue length up on the streaming workers.

Alex (Runtime): digging into kernel/queueing. early signs of KV cache dequant lock contention after the new quant scheme for key/value tensors. sequence-heavy sessions (seq > 1024) affected more.

Mike (ML Eng): yeah the new calib changes quantized embedding layers differently to save mem. probably increased dequant path latency under concurrent access.

Sara (SRE): severity = SEV2? customers impacted but partial. escalate if more customers. Anna, can you confirm SLA blips?

Anna (Oncall): Confirmed SLO breaches for streaming 5m window. CS put customers on notice. Thinking about routing mitigation — fallback to fp16 variant.

Alex (Runtime): Proposed mitigations:
- roll back calibration profile to int8-calib-2026-02 (previous)
- OR route streaming traffic to fp16 model variant redwood/gpt-small-fp16-2026-01 temporarily
- throttle batching/turn off continuous batching on streaming workers for hot sessions
- increase KV cache lock timeouts + flush stale KVs

Mike (ML Eng): Rollback is safest but takes a deploy/gencache refresh ~8-12m. Routing fallback can be near-instant. I'd start routing 20% then scale.

Sara (SRE): do it. Alex, start fallback routing. Ryan, prepare rollback instructions in case routing doesn't fully mitigate. I'll take first oncall handover notes.

deploy-bot: ACTION: routing-change started: set fallback model redwood/gpt-small-fp16-2026-01 for streaming-prod at 10% traffic.

Alex (Runtime): running command: \n```\nrclient route set --service streaming-prod --policy fallback --model redwood/gpt-small-fp16-2026-01 --percentage 10\n```\nWatching p99 now.

Ryan (Prod Eng): adding throttles to continuous batching on streaming workers: \n```\ninfractl update streaming-prod --continuous-batching=false --flush-interval=50ms\n```\nApplying to canary pool.

Sara (SRE): initial numbers: p95 back to baseline within 3m for the canary shards. p99 improved ~30% on canary. global still elevated.

Anna (Oncall): routing at 10% reduced customer tickets for those routed sessions but still seeing stalls for sessions that remained on int8. CS updated customers with temporary mitigations (reconnect, new session).

Mike (ML Eng): starting rollback plan (if routing doesn't stabilize). rollback steps: revert model profile to int8-calib-2026-02 in config-store then trigger config refresh on streaming pool. Command: \n```\nmodelctl set-calib redwood/gpt-small --profile int8-calib-2026-02 --env streaming-prod\nmodelctl refresh-config --service streaming-prod\n```\nEstimate 8-12m to be effective across all nodes.

Alex (Runtime): also found evidence of hotspot where dequant path was contending on a few nodes with high concurrent session count. I've evacuated two hot workers from pool and restarting them to clear locks.

Sara (SRE): I'm handing over to Anna in 15m. Notes: routing fallback active, continuous batching disabled on canary, rollback ready as step-2. See links: traces: https://tracing/trace/7890, metrics: https://metrics/query?p=streaming.p99

Anna (Oncall): taking over. I'll keep customers updated and coordinate escalations. if p99 doesn't drop below 2.5s in 10m, escalate to SEV1 and we roll full rollback.

deploy-bot: UPDATE: routing-change scaled to 40% traffic after monitoring checks.

Ryan (Prod Eng): after scaling to 40% p99 dropped further but still ~2.2s on overall. Most remaining high p99 are on long-lived sessions. I'm recommending a focused migration of long-lived sessions to fp16.

Mike (ML Eng): note — fp16 outputs slightly different numeric behavior but should be functionally OK for customers. will prepare QA note for CS on degradations.

Alex (Runtime): started selective migrate script to move sessions > 30s to fp16 fallback: \n```\nsession-migrate --service streaming-prod --criteria 'session_duration>30s' --target-model redwood/gpt-small-fp16-2026-01\n```\nMonitor for reconnection glitches.

Anna (Oncall): customer-impact update: CS reduced active escalations from 3 to 1. remaining one is high-volume enterprise with long sessions; we offered temporary routing to dedicated capacity.

Sara (SRE): status: mitigations holding. routing+batching change+evacuations reduced tail latency significantly. still tracking for full rollback if any regression appears. logging actions in incident tracker.

Mike (ML Eng): post-incident action items:
- root cause hypothesis: int8-calib-2026-03 introduced different quant alignment for KV tensors causing heavier dequant overhead and lock contention under concurrent sessions.
- reproduce in perf lab with concurrent session profile
- add pre-deploy perf gate for quant changes on streaming workloads
- ensure auto-fallback policy exists for long-lived sessions

Anna (Oncall): I'll set follow-up oncall rotation and schedule postmortem with SRE+ML+Runtime+CS. Postmortem draft in #postmortems in 24h.

Sara (SRE): handing back to Anna. I'm out. good work team. :raised_hands:

Anna (Oncall): closing handoff. monitoring for 30m then we downgrade alert if stable.

incidents-bot: NOTE: incident recorded as incident/2026-03-15-precision-bleed-1749123456. Severity: SEV2.
